waypoints.name: SR-20 Wine Spires pullout (milepost 166)
waypoints.note: Start of the steep climbers' trail toward Burgundy Col, the usual way down from Clean Break. The Silver Star Creek approach starts from a separate pullout about 8.5 miles east of Washington Pass.

waypoints.name: Juno Tower - Summit
waypoints.note: Clean Break, 15-pitch route on the east walls above Silver Star Creek.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the unsigned Wine Spires pullout on SR-20 near milepost 166 (~4,300 ft)

before.approach: From the pullout, find a faint boot path descending loose talus/scree to the east into the trees, passing a trail register, then crossing Early Winters Creek on a log (~4,080 ft). The trail climbs the timbered rib north of Burgundy Creek, steeply gaining elevation to a basin/camp bench around 6,500 ft (roughly 2 hours from the car), then continues up to Burgundy Col (~7,720 ft, ~3 hours). Good camping and a late-season spring are near 6,400-6,500 ft. For Clean Break this trail is the usual way down; the more direct way in to Juno Tower's east face is up Silver Star Creek from a separate pullout about 8.5 miles east of Washington Pass.

fitnessSpec.carToCar: ~8 hrs of climbing, plus the approach and descent

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~1.5–2 hrs via the east-side hairpin/Spire Gully (shared approach with neighboring routes, not fully route-specific-confirmed); descent is a downclimb plus 3 rappels down South Arete, ~1 hr
requiredSkills: Mixed dihedrals, thin slabs, flakes, and roofs
~20 bolts but still needs a real trad rack (doubles to 2", 60m rope)
One documented party needed an aider on a section — be ready for occasional aid if needed

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead (SR-20)
waypoints.note: Route is on the south/southeast face near Direct East Buttress; the route's name itself references hitchhiking back to a car left at the hairpin after descending the other side of the mountain.
